```{r, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

A tile map describes which small terrain image belongs at each position in
a grid. **shinyphaser** loads maps in [Tiled](https://www.mapeditor.org/) JSON
format through Phaser. These files can be generated programmatically, including
with LLM assistance, or exported from the Tiled editor using a compatible
configuration. The Swamps RPG map was created with LLM assistance.

This article builds a tiny room from two tiles.

## Start with a tiny room

Create an **8-by-6 room** with only two tile
IDs: **1 is floor** and **2 is wall**. Each tile is 64 pixels square. The room
has a border and two wall tiles in the middle:

```text
########
#......#
#..##..#
#......#
#......#
########
```

Here `.` means floor and `#` means wall. A small orange square will be the
player. The complete app, images, and JSON map are already provided in
`inst/examples/simple-map`, so no file-generation step or Tiled installation
is needed.

### Run the example

With shinyphaser installed, run this from the repository root:

```{r eval=FALSE, purl=FALSE}
shiny::runApp("inst/examples/simple-map")
```

The example contains:

```text
inst/examples/simple-map/
  app.R
  www/
    room.json
    floor.png
    wall.png
    player.png
```

`room.json` contains the 8-by-6 tile grid and two embedded tileset definitions.
Each tileset contains one image, and only the wall tile has the Boolean
property `collides = true`.

### How the app loads the map

The following code is the supplied **`inst/examples/simple-map/app.R`**:

```{r tiny-map-app, eval=FALSE}
library(shiny)
library(shinyphaser)

game <- PhaserGame$new(width = 512, height = 384)
ui <- tagList(tags$p("Arrow keys: move the orange square. Walls block movement."),
              game$use_phaser())

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  game <- PhaserGame$new(width = 512, height = 384)
  game$set_shiny_session(session)
  game$set_world_bounds(512, 384)
  game$add_map(
    map_key = "room", map_url = "room.json",
    tileset_urls = c("floor.png", "wall.png"),
    tileset_names = c("floor", "wall"), layer_name = "terrain"
  )
  player <- game$add_sprite(
    "player", "player.png", x = 96, y = 96,
    frame_width = 32, frame_height = 32, frame_count = 1, frame_rate = 1
  )
  player$add_player_controls(speed = 140)
  game$enable_terrain_collision("player")
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

Shiny serves the files in the app's `www/` folder, so the URLs above need no
extra resource-path setup. The first loaded map becomes active automatically.
The 512-by-384 canvas matches `8 * 64` by `6 * 64` pixels, and the player
starts in the center of the first interior floor tile.

Try moving across the floor and into both the border and the middle wall.
To change the room, edit the tile-data array in `www/room.json` (1 for floor,
2 for wall), or open that JSON file in Tiled, then restart the app. You now have the same basic ingredients as a larger map: tile IDs,
tileset images, a terrain layer, and an actor registered for terrain collision.
Phaser still loads from jsDelivr, so the browser needs Internet access.

### See the example in action

The orange square moves across the floor and stops at the room's border and
the wall in the middle:

```{r, echo=FALSE, out.width="512px", fig.alt="Orange player moving through a small tile map and colliding with walls"}
knitr::include_graphics("assets/simple_map_example.gif")
```
